wps.title: io refuses DacFx's xp_msver call before SqlClient sends it, and the read-only trace test runs dbchange as its own process
wps.brief: The operator ruled on 2026-10-20 (option A of the question this work package raised): io refuses DacFx's xp_msver call before SqlClient sends it, so R14 and V3_MILESTONES.md §4 row 17 stay at no EXEC. The facts measured in the interrupted wave (notes and a decompile under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/xp/): DacFx 170.5.96 sends `exec xp_msver @optname=N'Platform',@optname=N'WindowsVersion',@optname=N'ProcessorCount',@optname=N'PhysicalMemory',@optname=N'FileDescription'` from ReliableConnectionHelper.GetServerPropertiesFromConnection whenever SERVERPROPERTY('EngineEdition') is 1, 2, 3, 4 or 8 and its per-process MemoryCache 'ServerAndDatabaseInfo' (8-hour expiry, keyed DataSource:InitialCatalog, the login not in the key) has no entry; the values feed only DacFxOperationTelemetry, which dbchange turns off; the whole call sits inside catch (Exception). Measured as the published dbchange in its own process: read sends it twice (the database and master) and check drift twice. Io.Tests DriftTests.The_read_only_principal_sends_no_DML_no_DDL_and_no_EXEC_through_check_drift_and_read passed only because it runs dbchange in the test process, where the admin's GoldenProject.Publish had already filled the cache for those keys. Build: (1) in io, an observer on Microsoft.Data.SqlClient's DiagnosticListener (the 'SqlClientDiagnosticListener' source; the WriteCommandBefore event) that throws for exactly a stored-procedure call to xp_msver, or a text batch whose only statement is an EXEC of xp_msver, and lets every other command through; install it once per process before DacFx runs (where cli sets the telemetry opt-outs, or io's first database read; say why where you put it); the exception it throws names the refusal in io's error vocabulary so that, if a later DacFx stops catching it, the read fails as dacfx.failed naming the call, never silently. Read the prototype under scratchpad/xp/ first; it measured 0 probes, read exit 0 with a --json answer identical apart from run paths and elapsedMs, and check drift exit 0. (2) Tests first: a fast test of the matcher (xp_msver as a stored procedure and as `exec xp_msver ...` text refused; xp_instance_regread, sp_executesql, a SELECT and a procedure whose name merely contains xp_msver let through); and change the trace test, or add one beside it, so that it runs the published dbchange as its own process (as tests already do for read and diff through dist/dbchange) for the matching check drift, the drifted one and read --from env:dev, with the trace asserting zero EXEC of any kind, so that it fails if the probe returns. Keep the existing test's name if you change it in place (V3_PARITY.md and LAWS.md cite tests by name). (3) One DECISIONS.md line dated 2026-10-20 ending '· #705' recording the operator's choice, the mechanism and its failure mode. Safety: the observer must never swallow or alter any other command, never log a command's parameters, and never run for a connection dbchange does not open; it touches nothing on the server.

wps.title: io/AggregateQueries: one ScriptDom builder per precondition kind, none able to raise an error that carries a value
wps.startNotes: Built in the interrupted wave 4 as wp/2.3 (2ddb148), then fixed for its first round of findings as wp/2.3-r1 (98b21c5): the Check rewriter types comparison operands and uses TRY_CONVERT for implicit conversions; Fits counts over-length as violating only where ALTER COLUMN fails; PartitionRows checks every table the statement names; a collation is validated before any COLLATE is written; the property enumerates every type pair and re-reads Alone queries. Round one's must-fix findings were: Rewriter.Boolean's comparison handling in io/AggregateQueries.Check.cs; ColumnRef writing the collation as an unvalidated identifier in io/AggregateQueries.Trees.cs; PartitionRows in io/SqlServer.Allowlist.cs. Verify that each is fixed, and look for anything else.
wps.brief: Build WP 2.3 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§8; read its row in full, §3, §4 rows 17 and 20, §18's risk 'a value escaping in an error', WP 1.4's allowlist, and DECISIONS.md's lines that name WP 2.3, among them the operator's ruling 2.9 of 2026-09-25 on Fits and the 2026-10-19 lines on created columns and parent tables read in place). For each precondition kind WP 2.1a put in the kernel (kernel/Preconditions.cs: TableEmpty, NotNull, Fits, ForeignKey, Unique, Check; the statement-shown kinds come later), one ScriptDom builder in io/AggregateQueries that asks SQL Server rather than re-deriving: NotNull counts rows where the column is null; Fits counts rows whose value is not null and whose TRY_CONVERT to the new declared type (kernel/ColumnType.cs written as the target type) is null, plus, for a character or binary target, rows whose DATALENGTH of the converted value exceeds the new length in bytes; the query session sets LANGUAGE and DATEFORMAT to the Octopus login's defaults, unknown until spike S7, so commit us_english and mdy as the default, parameterized, with the provenance saying they are not verified against the Octopus step; a Fits site whose type changes into a character type prints a line that substituted characters are not counted, and one whose Scale falls a line that rounded values are not counted; ForeignKey counts child rows with every key column non-null and no parent; Unique counts groups over the key with more than one row under the constraint's own null semantics; Check counts rows where NOT (<CheckConstraint.Expression>) holds, which counts false and not unknown, an expression that converts being rewritten to its TRY_ form or the site reading 'not predictable read-only'. All of one table's claims, of every kind, are items of one SELECT, so each table is scanned once. From the Facsimile: Fits counts each value class as its own item (over length, over bytes, not convertible, lossy round trip, empty string to a non-string type, overflow), and Unique counts duplicate groups per collation class (exact, case, accent, trailing space, two NULLs) under the collation the index will be built with. TableEmpty may also be read from sys.partitions, which a VIEW DEFINITION-only login can read: that is exactly one new allowlist entry, with its negative case in the allowlist's fuzz corpus (tests/Golden/aggregate-queries/). Nothing else in the allowlist changes: the operator's later ruling on folded signatures belongs to WP 3.7, not here. Safety, held word for word to WP 1.4: every builder's output passes AggregateQuery.Of; no builder can produce CONVERT or CAST, only the TRY_ forms and length tests, so no query raises an error that quotes a value; a failed query against an environment classified real reports its error number and precondition only (Measure already withholds the message; prove it holds for these queries). Done when: every builder's output passes the allowlist; a fixture test per kind runs the builder against rows planted by plain INSERTs on a copy (LocalServer.Create) and the counts equal the planted counts, value class by value class and collation class by collation class; the pure cases of archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/cases/10-questions.md for these kinds pass, keeping their case identifiers in test names or InlineData. Update V3_PARITY.md's PAR-021 ('the queries — not held yet: WP 2.3') to name the tests, keeping law P's clause waiting on WP 4.5. Per-file budget: 500 lines a code file, 140 characters a line; Appendix F plans the reader, AggregateQueries.cs and Predict.cs at 690 in all.
